newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai maize and soymeal firm on supply tightness.
newsitem.headline: Thai maize and soymeal firm on supply tightness.

text.p: Thai domestic prices of maize/corn paid by feed producers continued to firm this week as fresh supplies entering the market were scarce, trade sources said on Tuesday.
The price of 14.50 percent-moisture maize was quoted at 4.28-4.40 baht (US17.0 cents) a kg, compared with 4.16-4.25 baht a kg a week ago, traders said.
They attributed the rise in prices to moonsoon rains which had affected transportation of the produce to Bangkok.
"The rain also dampened the corn, making it not immediately available for the market," said an official of the Thai Maize and Produce Traders Association.
Prices of locally-crushed soymeal from imported soymeal prices also rose to 10.05 baht a kg from 9.70-9.75 baht last week due to tight supply.

Soymeal stocks were diminishing as imported soymeal from Brazil for August and September shipment had yet to arrive in Bangkok, they said. Thai feed millers had ordered 50,000 tonnes of low quality soymeal from Brazil. The prices were said to be below US$300.00 C&F Bangkok.
